newsitem.title: USA: US adj retail sales up 1.6 pct w/e June 21 - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: US adj retail sales up 1.6 pct w/e June 21 - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 1.6 percent in the three weeks of fiscal June versus last month, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 8.1 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales advanced 7.9 percent in the week ended June 21, compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

Despite an improvement in seasonal merchandise as warm weather rolled in, total sales activity fell slightly below expectations for many of the surveyed retail stores, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
"(Retailers) are selling seasonal merchandise now. But, nevertheless, the results are a little disappointing," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"That means the regular merchandise isn't moving as well as they thought it would," he said.
Eilenberg said overall sales in June registered a "decent increase" over May.
As for the month, however, Redbook Research analyst projected final sales for the month to hit near the 7.4 percent level, down from retailers' 8.5-percent plans.
Sales of women's apparel continued to lag at the major discount stores, Eilenberg said. In the department stores and chain stores, home furnishings did not perform up to par, he said.
With two more weeks of retail sales' results for June, Eilenberg said, "I think it is going to taper off as the month concludes."
